options.B: 4.2 meters; only accessory structure height applies on ridgelines
options.C: 8.1 meters; Gorrath Ridgeline View Protection Policy applies above 350 m elevation
options.D: 8.5 meters; an averaging rule applies above 400 m
options.E: 9.5 meters; the Gorrath exception only applies below 350 m
options.F: 21.0 meters; R-3 rules apply above 400 m elevation

evidence: Structures on Gorrath Ridge parcels **above 350 m elevation** are subject to **8.1 meters** maximum (Exception R-1.2(b)).
reasoning: 420 m > 350 m threshold. The standard 9.5 m maximum is reduced. Option E misstates the threshold direction.

question: A senior housing development where 85% of occupants are age 65 or older is proposed in Zone R-2 on a 1.5-hectare lot. What is the maximum permitted number of dwelling units?

options.A: 36 units
options.B: 46 units
options.C: 48 units
options.D: 51 units
options.E: 56 units
options.F: 87 units

evidence: Senior housing (≥80% occupants age 65+) may develop at up to **34 du/ha**; 34 × 1.5 = **51 units**.
reasoning: Rule R-2.1 Exception R-2.1(b). This is the highest density allowed in R-2. Standard (24 × 1.5 = 36) and affordable-unit bonus (31 × 1.5 = 46.5 ≈ 46) are lower.

question: Why does Zone PO-1 restrict tree removal for trees with a DBH of 15 cm or greater?

options.A: To maintain impervious surface ratios below 22%
options.B: To protect the environmental character of the Lake Orvaine Reach overlay zone
options.C: To protect the shoreline setback from encroachment
options.D: To comply with the Orvaine Province Territorial Council requirements
options.E: To ensure noise attenuation from M-1 industrial uses across the lake
options.F: To maintain compliance with the Drasswell Common Flood Proofing Program

evidence: Rule PO-1.3 prohibits removal of trees ≥15 cm DBH without a Veltharrow Tree Removal Permit, consistent with the **environmental and mixed-use character** of Zone PO-1.
reasoning: Zone PO-1 is established for environmental and mixed-use character. The tree rule, impervious cap, and setback all serve this purpose; the specific tree rule is one component.

question: What is the stated reason for the Pellgate Special Height Overlay limiting R-3 buildings to 21.0 meters in Pellgate Flats?

options.A: Preservation of sight lines to the Veltharrow Civic Hall tower
options.B: Protection of the Lake Orvaine shoreline view corridor
options.C: Historic district conservation requirements
options.D: Stormwater runoff and flood mitigation concerns
options.E: Gorrath Ridgeline View Protection Policy
options.F: Aircraft approach path proximity

evidence: The Pellgate Special Height Overlay limits R-3 structures to 21.0 meters due to **aircraft approach path proximity**.
reasoning: Exception R-3.2(a) states this explicitly. Sight-line protection applies to Cornrath Square properties in C-3. The ridgeline policy applies to Gorrath Ridge.

question: Under Rule C-1.3, drive-through facilities are prohibited in C-1 zones. What is the status of a pharmacy drive-through that was in operation before Ordinance Z-2017-009's effective date?

options.A: It must close immediately
options.B: It may continue but must convert to no-contact delivery by 2030
options.C: It may expand by up to 20% of its original footprint per decade
options.D: It must apply for a Conditional Use Permit within 90 days
options.E: It is exempt because pharmacies are excluded from C-1 regulations
options.F: It may continue as a legal nonconforming use but may not expand

evidence: Exception C-1.3(a): pharmacies and financial service establishments operating drive-throughs as of the effective date of Ordinance Z-2017-009 are **legal nonconforming uses** and may continue operation indefinitely but may **not expand** the drive-through facility.
reasoning: No new drive-through permits are available under any circumstance (Exception C-1.3(b)), but existing ones are grandfathered without a time limit.

question: Under Zone R-3, which streets are designated as Pedestrian Priority Corridors triggering the ground-floor activation requirement?

options.A: Cornrath Avenue, Drasswell Road, and Orvaine Provincial Route 7
options.B: Cornrath Avenue, Fellwick Lane, and Cornrath Square
options.C: Cornrath Avenue, Municipal Lane, and Quorrath Street
options.D: Drasswell Road, Fellwick Lane, and Gorrath Ridge Drive
options.E: Cornrath Avenue, Drasswell Road, and Fellwick Lane
options.F: Drasswell Road, Orvaine Provincial Route 22, and Fellwick Bypass

evidence: The Pedestrian Priority Corridors are **Cornrath Avenue, Drasswell Road, and Fellwick Lane**.
reasoning: Rule R-3.3. Municipal Lane, Quorrath Street, and Civic Drive define the Cornrath Square plaza boundary (C-3 context), not the R-3 ground-floor corridors.

question: What is the maximum impervious surface coverage allowed in Zone PO-1 for any individual lot?
evidence: Total impervious surface in Zone PO-1 shall not exceed **22%** of any individual lot area.
reasoning: Rule PO-1.2. Option B (38%) is the R-1 maximum; option A (27%) is R-1's reduced Fellwick Creek adjacency limit; D (40%) is the permeable-paver counting factor.

question: Under Zone R-2, which exception allows the HIGHEST maximum building density, and what is that density?

options.A: Affordable-unit bonus (Exception R-2.1(a)): 31 du/ha
options.B: 100% affordable project (Exception R-3.1(a)): no cap
options.C: Mixed-use commercial ground floor (Exception R-3.1(b)): 102 du/ha
options.D: Standard maximum: 24 du/ha
options.E: Transit Node proximity (Exception R-2.2(a)): 34 du/ha
options.F: Senior housing (Exception R-2.1(b)): 34 du/ha

evidence: Senior housing (≥80% occupants age 65+) may develop at up to **34 du/ha**, the highest R-2 density exception.
reasoning: Rule R-2.1. The affordable-unit bonus allows 31 du/ha; senior housing allows 34 du/ha. The R-3 exceptions apply to a different zone.

question: Under Zone R-1, which impervious surface coverage limit is most restrictive, and where does it apply?

options.A: 27% on lots adjacent to Fellwick Creek within 30 meters of the centerline
options.B: 38% on all R-1 lots as the standard maximum
options.C: 22% in Zone PO-1 lots that overlap R-1
options.D: 40% on lots using permeable pavers
options.E: 27% on all Gorrath Ridge parcels above 350 m elevation
options.F: 20% within 55 meters of the SP-1 zone boundary

evidence: Exception R-1.5(b): lots **adjacent to Fellwick Creek within 30 meters of the centerline** have a reduced maximum impervious coverage of **27%**.
reasoning: Rule R-1.5. The standard maximum is 38% (option B). The 22% limit is PO-1 (option C). Permeable pavers count at 40% of their area toward the calculation, not as a separate limit.

question: Which zone has a development prohibition on all new habitable structures, with only public infrastructure and emergency flood response structures as exceptions?

options.A: PO-1, Lake Orvaine Reach Preservation Overlay
options.B: OS-1, Open Space and Parks
options.C: SP-1, Drasswell Flood Special Purpose
options.D: M-2, Heavy Industrial
options.E: R-1 within 30 meters of Fellwick Creek
options.F: M-1 in Wyndmere Spur industrial belt

evidence: Zone **SP-1** (Drasswell Flood Special Purpose): **No new habitable structure shall be constructed** within SP-1 (Rule SP-1.1).
reasoning: PO-1 restricts setbacks and impervious coverage but doesn't prohibit habitable structures entirely. SP-1 is the only zone with an outright habitable-structure prohibition.

question: Comparing the old and new values established by Ordinance Z-2017-009 for the Lake Orvaine Reach shoreline setback: by how many meters was the setback increased?

options.A: 10.5 meters
options.B: 12.0 meters
options.C: 15.0 meters
options.D: 13.5 meters
options.E: 8.5 meters
options.F: 14.0 meters

evidence: Old setback: 25.0 meters; new setback: 38.5 meters; increase = **13.5 meters**.
reasoning: Zone PO-1.1 and Ordinance Z-2017-009 Sub-Change B. 38.5 − 25.0 = 13.5 m.

question: In the C-3 District, what is the maximum building height for properties fronting directly on Cornrath Square, and how does it differ from the standard C-3 maximum?

options.A: Standard C-3 is 45.0 m; Cornrath Square frontage is 38.0 m — Cornrath Square is shorter
options.B: Standard C-3 is 38.0 m; Cornrath Square frontage is 45.0 m — Cornrath Square is taller
options.C: Both are 45.0 m; no exception applies to Cornrath Square
options.D: Standard C-3 is 45.0 m; Cornrath Square frontage is 21.0 m — the Pellgate overlay applies
options.E: Standard C-3 is 38.0 m; Cornrath Square frontage is 38.0 m — they are equal
options.F: Standard C-3 is 45.0 m; Cornrath Square frontage is 28.0 m — the R-3 standard applies

evidence: Standard C-3 maximum: **45.0 meters**. Cornrath Square frontage exception: **38.0 meters** to protect sight lines to the Veltharrow Civic Hall tower.
reasoning: Rules C-3.1 and C-3.1(a). The reduction applies specifically to sight-line protection. 21.0 m is the Pellgate Flats R-3 overlay, unrelated to C-3.

question: A lot in the R-1 District has an area of 580 square meters. An owner wants to add a detached accessory dwelling unit. What is the maximum permitted floor area for that ADU?

options.A: 74 square meters, because the standard maximum applies to all R-1 ADUs
options.B: 65 square meters, because lots under 600 sq m use the caretaker-unit limit
options.C: 84 square meters, because corner-lot exceptions expand ADU rights
options.D: 55 square meters, because lots under 600 sq m use the reduced ADU limit
options.E: 74 square meters, because the 580 sq m exceeds the 511 sq m pre-1955 minimum
options.F: No ADU is permitted on lots under 600 sq m

evidence: Exception R-1.4(a): ADUs on lots **smaller than 600 sq m** are limited to **55 square meters** of floor area.
reasoning: 580 < 600 sq m triggers the exception. The standard 74 sq m limit applies only to lots of 600 sq m or more.

question: A C-3 building has 40 linear meters of frontage on Cornrath Avenue. What is the maximum total signage area permitted under Rule C-3.4?

options.A: 40 square meters
options.B: 45 square meters
options.C: 20 square meters
options.D: 25 square meters
options.E: 35 square meters
options.F: 30 square meters

evidence: Maximum signage: **0.75 sq m per linear meter of frontage**; 40 m × 0.75 = **30 square meters**.
reasoning: Rule C-3.4. Option A applies a 1.0 sq m factor; option C applies 0.50 sq m; others use different multipliers.

question: A PO-1 lot has an area of 1,000 square meters and currently has 300 square meters of impervious surface. An owner proposes to add a 30-square-meter patio. May this proceed, and why?

options.A: No, because the proposed patio would bring impervious coverage to 33%, exceeding the 22% PO-1 cap
options.B: Yes, because 330 sq m is below the 38% limit for shoreline lots
options.C: Yes, because only structures within 38.5 m of the high-water mark require a permit
options.D: Yes, because the total would remain under 400 sq m, the PO-1 hard cap
options.E: No, because any new construction in PO-1 requires a water-dependent structures permit
options.F: Yes, provided the patio uses permeable pavers counted at 40%

evidence: Current impervious: 300/1,000 = **30%**, already exceeding the **22% PO-1 cap**. Adding 30 sq m would raise it to 33%, further violating the limit.
reasoning: Rule PO-1.2. The 22% cap applies lot-wide; 30% already violates it. The property is a legal nonconforming use and may not increase impervious coverage further.

question: An M-1 property in Wyndmere Spur holds Noise Variance Permit NVP-M1-2011-004. At 10:30 PM, what is the maximum sound level it may emit at its property line?

options.A: 71 dBA, because the variance permit allows this level at any hour
options.B: 62 dBA, because the daytime limit applies until midnight
options.C: 48 dBA, because the nighttime limit applies regardless of the variance permit
options.D: 55 dBA, because the variance increases the nighttime limit by 7 dBA
options.E: 71 dBA daytime only; after 10 PM the variance no longer applies, so 48 dBA governs
options.F: 62 dBA, because the daytime standard applies to variance holders at all hours

evidence: Exception M-1.2(a): Permit NVP-M1-2011-004 allows up to **71 dBA during daytime hours only**. After 10 PM, the standard nighttime limit of **48 dBA** applies.
reasoning: Rule M-1.2 and Exception M-1.2(a). The variance is restricted to daytime hours (7 AM–10 PM). 10:30 PM is outside those hours, so 48 dBA governs.

question: A new M-1 lot shares a 60-meter property line with a residential R-2 zone. A 9.5-meter-wide public alley separates them. What landscaping buffer is required along that shared line?

options.A: 8.5 meters of continuous landscaped buffer with one canopy tree per 6 linear meters
options.B: 4.0 meters of buffer, because the intervening alley of at least 9.0 meters reduces the requirement
options.C: No buffer required, because M-1 and R-2 are adjacent industrial and residential zones that are always exempt
options.D: 8.5 meters, because alley width must exceed 12.0 meters to qualify for the reduction
options.E: 4.0 meters only along the first 30 meters; 8.5 meters for the remainder
options.F: No buffer required, because M-1 abutting M-1 or M-2 is exempt and R-2 is treated equivalently

evidence: Exception M-1.3(a): where a **public alley or road right-of-way of at least 9.0 meters** separates M-1 from a residential zone, the buffer may be reduced to **4.0 meters**.
reasoning: Rule M-1.3. The alley is 9.5 m ≥ 9.0 m, so the reduction applies. Option D invents a 12.0 m threshold not in the document.

question: A new construction project in Drasswell Common is planned on a lot whose boundary is 45 meters from the nearest SP-1 zone boundary. What minimum lowest habitable floor elevation must it meet?

options.A: The rule does not apply; 45 meters exceeds the 30-meter threshold
options.B: 98.2 m AMSL — base flood elevation plus 0.8 m
options.C: 97.9 m AMSL — the old pre-2019 standard
options.D: 97.4 m AMSL — the base flood elevation itself
options.E: The rule does not apply; only properties within 30 meters of SP-1 must comply
options.F: 98.4 m AMSL — an additional 0.2 m safety margin applies within 50 meters

evidence: Rule SP-1.2 applies to **properties within 55 meters of an SP-1 zone boundary**. 45 m < 55 m, so the minimum habitable floor is **98.2 m AMSL** (97.4 + 0.8).
reasoning: Rule SP-1.2. Options A and E invent a 30-meter threshold. Option C uses the superseded 2012 standard. Option F invents an additional margin.

question: A bakery in the C-1 District wishes to begin dough preparation at 4:00 AM. Is this permitted, and on what condition?

options.A: Yes, with no restrictions, because food preparation is exempt from C-1 operating hours
options.B: No, because C-1 operating hours begin at 6:00 AM with no exceptions for food establishments
options.C: Yes, but only if the bakery holds a Veltharrow Late-Night Commercial Permit
options.D: Yes, provided no customer-facing operations commence before 6:00 AM
options.E: No, because food preparation must begin no earlier than 4:30 AM under the C-1 exception
options.F: Yes, but only between 4:30 AM and 5:30 AM — beyond that requires a special permit

evidence: Exception C-1.2(b): bakeries may begin operations at **4:30 AM**, not 4:00 AM, provided no customer-facing operations commence before 6:00 AM.
reasoning: 4:00 AM is earlier than the 4:30 AM exception allows. Option D correctly states the customer-facing condition but misses that 4:00 AM is still too early.

question: An R-3 building under 8 units fronts entirely on a side street with no Pedestrian Priority Corridor frontage. Is it subject to the ground-floor activation requirement?

options.A: No, because buildings without Pedestrian Priority Corridor frontage are exempt under Exception R-3.3(a)
options.B: No, because buildings under 8 units are exempt under Exception R-3.3(b)
options.C: Yes, because all R-3 buildings must provide 65% active use regardless of street type
options.D: Yes, but only for the ground-floor units facing the side street
options.E: No, because side-street buildings use the C-1 commercial activation rule instead
options.F: Yes, but the threshold is reduced to 30% of frontage for side-street buildings

evidence: Exception R-3.3(a): buildings with **frontage entirely on side streets** and not on Pedestrian Priority Corridors are **exempt** from the ground-floor activation requirement.
reasoning: Two exemptions exist: R-3.3(a) (side-street frontage) and R-3.3(b) (under 8 units). Either alone suffices here; the question identifies both apply, but A is correct due to R-3.3(a) applying first.

options.A: Ordinance Z-1987-001, effective January 1, 1988
options.B: Ordinance C-2005-001, effective July 1, 2005

question: A mixed-use R-3 building in Pellgate Flats has ground-floor commercial space equal to 45% of its ground floor area. What density bonus, if any, applies under Rule R-3.1(b)?

options.A: No bonus applies; R-3.1(b) only covers affordable housing
options.B: 15 additional units per hectare above the 87 du/ha base maximum
options.C: 31 du/ha applies as under the R-2 affordable-unit exception
options.D: No bonus applies in Pellgate Flats because the height overlay supersedes density rules
options.E: 15 additional units per hectare, but the Pellgate height overlay still caps the building at 21.0 m
options.F: 87 du/ha plus 34 units per hectare for mixed use

evidence: R-3.1(b) grants **15 additional units per hectare** for ≥40% ground-floor commercial. The **Pellgate Special Height Overlay** (21.0 m) applies independently and still caps the building.
reasoning: Ground-floor commercial is 45% ≥ 40%, so R-3.1(b) triggers the density bonus. However, the height overlay from Ordinance Z-2017-009 applies to all R-3 structures in Pellgate Flats regardless of the density provision.
